Cardiovascular analysis - CVD – A global health crisis - BEATLAB Cardiovascular Diseases Early detection About us Select Page Revolutionizing cardiovascular analysis Early CVD detection made accessible – advanced cardiovascular modeling for clinical precision Contact us CVD – A global health crisis Cardiovascular disease (CVD) claims 18 million lives each year, making it the world’s leading cause of death. Over 500 million people live with CVD globally, yet current diagnostic tools fail to detect disease early enough, leaving many undiagnosed until life-threatening symptoms appear. Contact us 80% of cases could be prevented Up to 80% of CVDs are preventable with early detection and intervention. Yet current diagnostic tools lack either the precision or accessibility needed for effective screening, leaving millions undiagnosed until severe symptoms appear. PAD: the silent pandemic For a lesser-known CVD, Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD), over 230 million people worldwide are affected – many without symptoms. Because current methods detect only symptomatic cases, early disease is often missed, leading to preventable harm. $1 trillion crisis by 2030 CVDs will cost society over 1 trillion USD annually by 2030. Late diagnosis drives these costs, a single stroke costs $122,000 per admission and PAD treatment costs $7,000 per patient yearly. Early detection and prevention is both lifesaving and cost-effective. CVDs – A global health crisis Contact us Of deaths per year globally Million affected % Without symptoms The fact is that it doesn’t have to be this way, up to 80% CVDs are preventable with early detection and intervention. The problem is that there are no readily available methods for early and precise detection of CVD signs. BEATLAB changes this. Advanced cardiovascular modeling for clinical precision BEATLAB transforms accessible pulse wave measurements into comprehensive cardiovascular analysis. Using proprietary signal processing and physics-based cardiovascular modeling, we identify and locate arterial stenosis and other cardiovascular anomalies before symptoms appear, with high accessibility and at a fraction of the cost of medical imaging technologies. 1. Identifies cardiovascular anomalies long before symptoms appear and when intervention is most effective. 2. Delivers detailed cardiovascular insights comparable to medical imaging, but accessible for primary care screening. 3. Works with standard diagnostic devices, no expensive new hardware required. Analysis results provided in a couple of minutes. How BEATLAB works step by step 1. Measure: Non-invasive pulse wave measurements using standard PPG sensors at multiple body locations. Fast (<5 minutes), and accessible in any clinical setting. 2. Model: Combining proprietary signal processing and physics-based cardiovascular modeling to create a digital twin of the patient’s cardiovascular system, revealing detailed hemodynamic parameters. 3. Detect and locate: AI-powered analysis identifies and pinpoints cardiovascular anomalies and early CVD signs, providing actionable clinical insights for targeted intervention. What makes BEATLAB unique Beyond surrogate markers Not just blood pressure or pulse wave velocity – comprehensive cardiovascular system analysis. Clinical-grade from accessible sensors Medical imaging-level insights without expensive equipment. Localization, not just detection Pinpoints anomaly location for precise intervention. About us Three co-founders, one mission: making early cardiovascular disease detection accessible to everyone. Driven by personal experiences with CVD, we bring together expertise in cardiovascular modeling, biosignals, AI, and medical device commercialization to transform how CVD is detected and prevented. Daniel Adin, COO & Co-founder Leads data science and AI development, architecting the machine learning and digital twin modeling that power BEATLAB’s cardiovascular analysis. Co-founder Escenda Engineering. Mikael Karlsson, CTO & Co-founder Inventor of BEATLAB technology and lead researcher. PhD in Flow Acoustics (KTH), co-founder Escenda Engineering. Pioneering the cardiovascular modeling methodology enabling early CVD detection from pulse wave analysis. Pontus Axblom, CEO & Co-founder Leads strategy, operations, and business development. Former CEO Bohus Biotech, medical device regulatory consultant, software developer and ex-Accenture. Deep expertise in medical device commercialization and regulatory pathways. Through cardiovascular modeling and AI, we are transforming how CVD is detected and prevented, before symptoms appear. Reach out to learn more. Please make sure to always clearly state who you are, so that we can be certain that we do not modify or delete any data of the wrong person. 9. Cookie Policy (EU) - BEATLAB Cardiovascular Diseases Early detection About us Select Page Cookie Policy (EU) This Cookie Policy was last updated on 06.02.2026 and applies to citizens and legal permanent residents of the European Economic Area and Switzerland. 1. Introduction Our website, https://beatlab.se (hereinafter: "the website") uses cookies and other related technologies (for convenience all technologies are referred to as "cookies"). Cookies are also placed by third parties we have engaged. In the document below we inform you about the use of cookies on our website. 2. What are cookies? A cookie is a small simple file that is sent along with pages of this website and stored by your browser on the hard drive of your computer or another device. The information stored therein may be returned to our servers or to the servers of the relevant third parties during a subsequent visit. 3. What are scripts? A script is a piece of program code that is used to make our website function properly and interactively. This code is executed on our server or on your device. 4. What is a web beacon? A web beacon (or a pixel tag) is a small, invisible piece of text or image on a website that is used to monitor traffic on a website. In order to do this, various data about you is stored using web beacons. 5. Cookies 5.1 Technical or functional cookies Some cookies ensure that certain parts of the website work properly and that your user preferences remain known. By placing functional cookies, we make it easier for you to visit our website. This way, you do not need to repeatedly enter the same information when visiting our website and, for example, the items remain in your shopping cart until you have paid. We may place these cookies without your consent. 5.2 Statistics cookies We use statistics cookies to optimize the website experience for our users. With these statistics cookies we get insights in the usage of our website. We ask your permission to place statistics cookies. 5.3 Marketing/Tracking cookies Marketing/Tracking cookies are cookies or any other form of local storage, used to create user profiles to display advertising or to track the user on this website or across several websites for similar marketing purposes. 5.4 Social media On our website, we have included content from Facebook and LinkedIn to promote web pages (e.g. “like”, “pin”) or share (e.g. “tweet”) on social networks like Facebook and LinkedIn. This content is embedded with code derived from Facebook and LinkedIn and places cookies. This content might store and process certain information for personalized advertising. Please read the privacy statement of these social networks (which can change regularly) to read what they do with your (personal) data which they process using these cookies. The data that is retrieved is anonymized as much as possible. Facebook and LinkedIn are located in the United States. 6.
